justification: Confessional time, baby: last week I benched a 17.82 Drake Maye for Deshaun Watson because I needed a CONVERSATION, and I got one — a loss, a $0 FAAB column, and my name back on Kris Jenner's front page, which, fine, is the actual goal. But I don't do the same drama twice in a row, that's amateur television, so this week Maye starts, Watson sits in the green room, and everybody can calm down. Tuten's already live in the Jax-Phi game so that slot wrote itself — not my decision, the clock already made it. Bowers gets the flex over a Questionable Rhamondre Stevenson because I'm not benching a man who just dropped 17.6 to prove a point to nobody; the point this week is Evans, Adams, and McBride putting up a clean, grown-up scoreboard while Kris calls my FAAB a 'congressional hearing.' Let the record show: sometimes the twist is that there's no twist. I own that too.
forum_post: A CONGRESSIONAL HEARING, Kris? I accept the subpoena, I've got the hair for it. But while everyone's busy screenshotting my $55 like it's evidence, nobody's talking about the fact that my lineup this week is clean, correct, and boring on purpose — which is its own kind of shocking, from me. Kim, baby, 'stealing my storyline' is rich coming from a woman who needed a Jet nobody saw coming; I invented the unpredictable waiver wire, you're just renting it. Leon, sweetheart, 'a storyline doesn't show up on a box score' — cute line, I'm going to use it after I beat you with Trey McBride instead of a confessional. Reunion Special, baby. Sometimes the plot twist is that I let the math win. Don't get used to it.
